text:
lina-cs: Hey SREs, multiple customers (Acme + BetaInc) reporting 503s and timeouts to hosted inference around 10:10 UTC. CS call with Acme in 30m. sample request_id=req_9ab3f, logs attached from their side show 503 gateway errors. can we triage?

maya-sre: Looking now. Noticed a spike of pod restarts in hosted-gpu-pool-usw2 at ~10:08. Events show OOMKilled then container restart. kube events: 
```
Pod hosted-infer-4f7b  OOMKilled  10:08:46
Pod hosted-infer-4f7b  BackOff    10:09:01
```

devon-eng: any crashlogs / segfault traces? I pulled one worker core dump from node gpunode-12: shows SIGSEGV in attention kernel, stack hints at nvml/cuMemcpyAsync failing while allocating KV cache.

arnav-ml: We rolled a quantized model swap to v2-quant at 10:05 (canary), might be heavier on VRAM in worst-case long-context streams. Could be interaction with driver pinned pages.

maya-sre: Repro steps I'm running locally: large-context streaming (20k tokens), dynbatch enabled, concurrency 24 -> worker OOMs under sustained 70% GPU utilization. Quick check of nvidia-smi: 
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Processes:                                                       GPU Memory |
| 0   python                                                      31240MiB |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

devon-eng: Do we have the exact node driver vs container CUDA mismatch? I see nodes on 520.xx and some containers built with 525 libraries. That can cause memory fragmentation leading to OOM amplification.

deploy-bot: deploy "model-swap/v2-quant" by devon-eng rolled at 2024-11-12T10:05:12Z (commit abcdef123) :rocket:

lina-cs: Acme says this started immediately after ~10:06. They were on long streaming calls, lots of tool calls. They want ETA and workaround.

maya-sre: Short-term mitigations: 1) disable dynbatch for affected pool (reduces memory multiplexing), 2) pin traffic away from GPU pool to cpu-fallback for critical customers (fallback routing), 3) scale up pool to add headroom. I'm pushing an emergency autoscaler policy to add 2 nodes to hosted-gpu-pool-usw2.

devon-eng: Technical mitigation we can patch quickly: revert quant swap for canary -> redeploy previous model image (v2-fp16) and restrict concurrency per worker to 12. Patch PR ready: revert-quant-hotfix (tests small).

arnav-ml: Also recommend rolling back the quantized KV-cache tweak from yesterday; it increases prefetch size. Will open rollback PR.

maya-sre: For triage please collect: pod name, dmesg, container logs (stderr), nvml logs, nvidia-smi output at time of crash, and core dump. Commands: 
```
kubectl -n hosted logs <pod> --previous
dmesg | tail -n 200
/opt/nvidia/bin/nvidia-smi -q -x
journalctl -u kubelet --since "10:00" --until "10:15"
```

devon-eng: I'll prepare the rollback and a canary exclusion rule to keep acme/betaInc on older model until we validate. ETA 20m to push rollback and reduce concurrency limit.

jamie-ps: Noted for CS: telling Acme we are diagnosing; provisional workaround: route their requests to fallback CPU cluster (slower but stable). Will propose 1 hour rollback ETA and ask if they can accept fallback for the call.

lina-cs: thanks. please post when rollback started and when stable so I can update customer.

maya-sre: Rollback started at 10:35 UTC (k8s rollout revert). Observed pods stabilizing, no further OOMKilled events after 10:44. Monitoring shows error rate falling toward baseline.

deploy-bot: rollback "model-swap/v2-quant" completed (deploy-id revert-2024-11-12-1035) :white_check_mark:

devon-eng: Confirmed: reverted to v2-fp16, concurrency cap applied to 12. Will keep dynbatch disabled for hosted-gpu-pool-usw2 for 2h while we gather heap dumps and run stress tests.

maya-sre: Follow-up actions: collect heap/core dumps for postmortem, run mem-fragmentation profiling, add healthcheck to detect progressive VRAM usage spike (preemptively drain), and add a canary gating metric for quant model swaps (GPU mem per-request p95).

arnav-ml: I'll run bench tests on v2-quant with driver 525 in staging to verify memory pattern. Might need to re-tune KV prefetch thresholds.

jamie-ps: CS updated Acme: offered fallback routing and rollback ETA; they accepted fallback for the call. Closing the urgent customer call.

lina-cs: excellent, please leave a short postmortem note when available and tag support.

maya-sre: Will open an incident postmortem with timelines, root cause hypothesis (quant swap + driver mismatch + dynbatch memory amplification -> GPU OOM -> container restart -> 503s), and action items.

devon-eng: Adding PR links and logs to incident doc.

lina-cs: thanks team :heart:
